name: analytics_project
description: Control scenario: twelve events from a realistic analytics-project agent stream, six topics that are LEXICALLY DISTINCT (auth, database, deploy, frontend, monitoring, billing). Measured pairwise cosines on bge-small-en-v1.5: same-topic pairs span [0.778, 0.937] median 0.915; cross-topic pairs span [0.320, 0.617] median 0.465. Clean gap of 0.162 — any threshold in (0.617, 0.778) gives 100%. This scenario exists to confirm that engram's consolidation loop works when the embedder is on its side, and to function as a regression guard: any change to consolidation must not drop this scenario below 100%.

events.text: The team enabled OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for the mobile clients and turned off password-based login in the admin panel last sprint.
OAuth 2.0 with PKCE is now the only supported authentication flow on mobile; passwords are deprecated in the admin UI.
PostgreSQL 16 was chosen over SQLite for the analytics warehouse because the expected write concurrency exceeds two hundred connections per second.
The analytics warehouse runs on PostgreSQL 16; the SQLite option was ruled out because of write concurrency above two hundred connections per second.
Blue-green deployments on Kubernetes via ArgoCD replaced the previous Jenkins pipeline after three production incidents in January.
The team switched from Jenkins to ArgoCD for blue-green Kubernetes deploys after January's three incidents.
The React Native app is migrating from Redux to Zustand for state management because the boilerplate was slowing feature delivery.
Zustand replaced Redux in the React Native app — the Redux boilerplate was the main bottleneck for feature delivery.
Grafana dashboards now show p99 latency per endpoint, backed by Prometheus scraping every fifteen seconds.
We added p99 latency per endpoint to Grafana; Prometheus scrapes the metrics every fifteen seconds.
Stripe replaced the in-house billing service because refund handling and subscription proration were taking three engineers per quarter to maintain.
The in-house billing service was retired in favor of Stripe; refund and proration logic was costing three engineer-quarters per year.

queries.question: why did the team switch away from Jenkins for deployments?
which database did we pick for the analytics warehouse and why?
how did we reduce React Native state management boilerplate?
what happened to the in-house billing code?
